title: QURAN-MD: A Fine-Grained Multilingual Multimodal Dataset of the Quran
base_benchmarks: Quran Recitations for Audio Classification dataset
findings: The paper identifies a critical gap in existing resources for Quranic studies, noting that they are often fragmented, focusing on either text or audio, and rarely combine modalities at both verse and word levels. The main contribution is the creation and release of QURAN-MD, a comprehensive, fine-grained, multimodal dataset that unifies Arabic text, English translation, phonetic transliteration, and aligned audio from 32 different reciters at both the verse and word levels. This new dataset is intended to support a wide range of computational research in natural language processing, speech technology, and digital Islamic studies.

measurement_description: The paper does not present a benchmark to measure model performance, but rather introduces a new dataset (QURAN-MD) intended to enable future research and benchmarking. The dataset is designed to facilitate computational analysis and modeling of the Quranic text and its oral recitation traditions, supporting tasks such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) for recitation, tajweed (recitation rules) detection, text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis, and pronunciation tutoring.
